newsitem.title: USA: Pension funds tell ADM holders to wait on proxy.
newsitem.headline: Pension funds tell ADM holders to wait on proxy.

text.p: Two large U.S. pension funds Thursday asked Archer Daniels Midland Co. shareholders not to sign and return proxy voting cards for the agribusiness company's annual meeting until the funds can send out materials justifying their proposal to change the company's bylaws.

The California Public Employees' Retirement System and the Florida Retirement System Trust Fund have proposed a change in the company's bylaws requiring ADM's board be composed of a majority of independent directors.
The push for independent directors comes in the wake of a probe by the Justice Department into alleged price-fixing by the company in the lysine, citric acid and high-fructose corn syrup market.

In the proxy materials filed in advance of the Oct. 17 meeting, ADM said the company has been informed that executive officers Michael Andreas and Terrance Wilson, as well as the company, are targets of the lysine investigation and that indictments are being considered against them.

ADM has proposed cutting its board to 12 members from 17, with three outside directors. In a letter to shareholders dated Thursday, ADM Chairman Dwayne Andreas said the company has tried to strike a balance between investors concerns about board independence and ADM's desire to find the best qualified candidates.

Calpers, which owns about 3.5 million shares of the Decatur, Illinois-based agribusiness giant, and the Florida trust, which holds about 3 million shares, said the warning was faxed to about half of ADM's shareholders and that they will respond to the proxy materials shortly.
